title: Descent of the special-chart elimination substitution
statement: For prepared Popescu data d, compatible c and cmod, and hc identifying the original variables, the unlocalized quotient D0=d.liftingAlgebra/(pi) admits a C0-algebra homomorphism to P=MvPolynomial (E k) (C0[1/a0]), sending each free auxiliary generator indexed by E k to its polynomial variable. Here C0=Cbar/(pi), D0 has its C0-algebra structure from cmod, and a0 is the class of epsilon(reduced(a k)). This statement constructs only the map out of the unlocalized quotient; it does not assert a retraction of the special-chart map or injectivity.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 07CP, displayed calculation modulo pi and comparison of chart coefficients; read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CP on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Construct the coefficient ring homomorphism s from R[x] to P=(Cbar/pi)[1/a_k][Z_j:j in E_k] by reduction, epsilon, quotient and localization. The specified kernel makes every f_l vanish, and pi vanishes. Choose the inverse of the unit s(a_k). Define z_j=X_j on E_k, and otherwise z_l=s(a_k) inverse times sum s(h_klj) X_j. Normalization verifies s(a_k) z_l=sum s(h_klj) z_j for every l, including l in E_k. Extend to a polynomial evaluation ev on R[x,z].

Import all Sheaf.RingTheory.PopescuLiftChartComparison and apply its existing private proved theorem Algebra.PopescuLiftPresentation.chart_coefficient_clearing. For each j in E_k it gives a_k^N b_j in the ideal generated by the f_l and C(pi squared), where b_j=a_kprime h_klj-sum h_kprime,ljprime h_k,jprimej. The coefficient map s kills that ideal. Since s(a_k) is a unit, cancel its N-th power to obtain s(b_j)=0. Multiply the evaluated kprime-th relation by s(a_k), use the k-th relations and interchange the finite sums. The result is sum s(b_j) z_j=0; cancel the unit. Thus ev kills every defining equation. No duplicate coefficient-clearing theorem is introduced.

Use the span universal property and Ideal.Quotient.lift to descend ev through the defining ideal, compose with ULift.ringEquiv, and descend through the quotient by pi. Compare the two R-algebra maps from R[x] to D0: c composed with epsilon and reduction, and the canonical quotient map composed with includeX. Polynomial algebra homomorphism extensionality and hc show equality. Surjectivity of epsilon and polynomial reduction then show g(c(b)) is the coefficient image of every b in Cbar. Quotient surjectivity and hcmod give the C0-algebra compatibility. Package the descended ring homomorphism as an algebra homomorphism. Evaluation on each free auxiliary variable is X_j by construction. The construction uses only units and finite sums and therefore covers empty E_k and zero coefficient localizations.

lean.statement:
theorem popescu_special_chart_substitution (R : Type a) (Cbar : Type c)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing Cbar] [Algebra R Cbar] (π : R)
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) Cbar]
    [IsScalarTower R (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) Cbar]
    (d : PopescuLiftPresentation R Cbar π) (hd : d.Prepared)
    (c : Cbar →ₐ[R] (d.liftingAlgebra ⧸
      Ideal.span ({algebraMap R d.liftingAlgebra π} : Set d.liftingAlgebra)))
    (cmod : (Cbar ⧸ Ideal.span ({algebraMap R Cbar π} : Set Cbar)) →+*
      (d.liftingAlgebra ⧸
        Ideal.span ({algebraMap R d.liftingAlgebra π} : Set d.liftingAlgebra)))
    (hc : ∀ i : Fin d.n, c (d.ε (MvPolynomial.X i)) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (d.x i))
    (hcmod : cmod.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk _) = c.toRingHom) (k : Fin d.r) :
    let C₀ := Cbar ⧸ Ideal.span ({algebraMap R Cbar π} : Set Cbar)
    let D₀ := d.liftingAlgebra ⧸
      Ideal.span ({algebraMap R d.liftingAlgebra π} : Set d.liftingAlgebra)
    letI := cmod.toAlgebra
    let A := Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk
      (Ideal.span ({algebraMap R Cbar π} : Set Cbar)) (d.ε (d.reduced (d.a k))))
    ∃ g : D₀ →ₐ[C₀] MvPolynomial (d.E k) A,
      ∀ j : d.E k, g (Ideal.Quotient.mk _
        (ULift.up (Ideal.Quotient.mk d.definingIdeal (MvPolynomial.X (.inr j.1))))) =
          MvPolynomial.X j
